markdown_report:
**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Training margins measure sampled-pair separation, not HR@10. Their scale and negative distribution complicate checkpoint comparisons. (2) Feedback favors recent, repeated interests over broad affinity. This motivates a recency hypothesis, but does not establish unmet need or compatibility. (3) The compatibility interface permits controlled architecture changes. Existing probes must still reach the actual trained module and distinguish missing observations from healthy results.

**Insights from related work.** (1) [Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) establish that sampled evaluation can misrank recommenders. Preserve the pinned objective and treat auxiliary rankings as diagnostics. (2) [Scarcelli et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.03606) demonstrate recommendation sensitivity to history edits. Such sensitivity measures model dependence, not causal preference. (3) [Liu et al.](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748042) identify availability confounding in arbitrary shuffling. Prefer matched deletion controls and avoid interpreting perturbations as behavioral ground truth.

**Directions and framework.** Organize research around objective alignment, temporal evidence, and metadata support:

| Direction | Existing signal | Gap | Proposed extension |
|---|---|---|---|
| Objective alignment | Training margins | Candidate and scale dependence | Pinned validation plus paired user bootstrap |
| Temporal evidence | SASRec sequence features | Unmeasured recency dependence | Recency residual and matched ablations |
| Metadata support | Titles/descriptions | Uncertain functional relationships | Evidence spans with abstention |

**Candidate algorithms.** Scores are originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

1. **Matched history-ablation adapter — 4/7/3.** Compare recent-history removal with equal-size random removal using fixed candidates [Scarcelli; Liu]. Originality: useful controlled combination, but established perturbation methods. Potential: exposes temporal dependence, but cannot establish relevance. Difficulty: reuses inference, but padding and position controls require care.
2. **Gated recency residual — 4/7/4; selected.** Mix SASRec features with an exponentially weighted history embedding. Originality: connects explicit recency with diagnostic testing, but both components are familiar. Potential: directly tests the feedback hypothesis, but may suppress durable interests. Difficulty: a small model change, but training, predictor serialization, and probes must agree.
3. **Evidence-supported metadata reranking — 5/6/6.** Add bounded title/description similarity to recent interests and abstain when evidence is missing. Originality: evidence-aware combination, but lexical reranking is established. Potential: improves inspectability, but similarity cannot establish compatibility. Difficulty: uses available text, but extraction and calibration expand scope.

**Selected implementation.** At 0% progress, test the small recency residual first. For every valid training position, compute causal exponentially weighted item embeddings, project them to the encoder dimension, and blend with SASRec using one learned scalar gate per category. Initialize toward SASRec and preserve its scoring function and loss.

`h = SASRec(seq); r = causal_exp_pool(item_emb(seq)); z = (1−sigmoid(a))*h + sigmoid(a)*project(r); score = z @ item_emb.T`

Retain all four routes, prescribed seeds, environment DATA_DIR, and trial-local artifacts. Update the predictor writer and compatibility view together. Preserve both diagnostic entry points; report valid counts and unavailable categories explicitly. Select exclusively by pinned macro validation HR@10; use matched ablations as supporting evidence.

idea.description: Add a causal, exponentially weighted history residual to each category's SASRec model, controlled by a learned scalar gate and evaluated with matched history ablations.
idea.motivation: Qualitative feedback suggests that recent, repeated interests sometimes receive insufficient weight. An explicit recency component provides a small, testable intervention while retaining the baseline sequence encoder.
idea.implementation_notes: Compute the residual at every training position using only its causal prefix. Exclude padding from the weighted normalization and return zero for empty prefixes. Use a small fixed decay grid within the shared budget; initialize the gate toward SASRec. Preserve baseline scoring and loss initially to isolate the architectural effect. Keep DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, all four dataset routes, and the SASREC_EPOCHS environment default of 200. Serialize decay, gate, projection, and model configuration beneath the trial directory, and update the predictor writer accordingly. DiagnosisProbe must invoke view.model.eval(), retain run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and return metrics with definitions; diagnosis_interpreter_prompt must incorporate both. Empty samples must be marked unavailable rather than interpreted as healthy. Metadata categories, ratings, review text, ownership, unmet need, and simulator traits must not be inferred. Compare against the baseline using only pinned validation macro HR@10; paired bootstrap intervals describe user uncertainty conditional on fixed candidates and trained models.
idea.pseudocode:
For each category:
  Initialize baseline SASRec, projection P, and scalar gate a favoring baseline.
  For each training batch:
    h = SASRec.log2feats(sequence)
    r = causal exponentially weighted mean of nonpadding item embeddings
    z = (1 - sigmoid(a)) * h + sigmoid(a) * P(r)
    Optimize baseline loss using z and baseline item scoring.
  Write checkpoint and matching predictor implementation.
  Evaluate using the pinned validation procedure.
  Diagnose fixed-candidate score/rank changes under recent deletion and equal-size random deletion, controlling padding and positions.
Select the configuration with highest macro validation HR@10.

originality.positive: Combines an explicit temporal inductive bias with controlled diagnostics tied to a concrete failure hypothesis.
originality.negative: Recency pooling and gated residual mixtures are established techniques; novelty is mainly the experimental integration.

future_potential.positive: Provides a simple basis for studying when explicit recency complements sequence attention across domains.
future_potential.negative: Validation gains may be dataset-specific, and temporal sensitivity alone cannot demonstrate better relevance.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires only causal pooling, a projection, and a scalar gate alongside the existing encoder.
code_difficulty.negative: Correct causal masking, predictor serialization, and compatible diagnostic features require coordinated changes.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Establishes inconsistency between sampled recommendation metrics and full-catalog model rankings.
limitations: Does not establish that improving auxiliary margins or full-catalog diagnostics improves this pinned sampled benchmark.

related_work.title: Scarcelli et al. (2025): sequence-edit recommendation explanations
contributions: Uses searches over sequence edits to examine changes in recommendations, as described in the supplied research summary.
limitations: Model fidelity and sensitivity do not identify causal user preferences or prove recommendation relevance.

related_work.title: Liu et al. (RecSys 2025): availability effects in history shuffling
contributions: Identifies item-availability confounding in arbitrary sequence shuffling, according to the supplied research summary.
limitations: Controlling availability does not resolve every ambiguity in interpreting history perturbations.
